title: The return (Ezra 1)
hook: Cyrus of Persia lets the exiles go home to rebuild

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last chapter of Daniel: the wise shine as the firmament, and those who turn many to righteousness, as the stars. Your line was shine as the firmament. What did you teach, and to whom? Day eight hundred seventy-four.

"Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia." A proclamation goes out through a whole empire, spoken aloud and put in writing. The God of heaven, says the king, has given him all the kingdoms of the earth, and charged him to build a house in Jerusalem, in Judah. Then the line that opens the way home. In the King James words: "Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem." After all the chapters of loss, the book of Ezra opens with a door.
screen: `A PROCLAMATION FROM CYRUS.` → `BUILD A HOUSE IN JERUSALEM.` → `LET HIM GO UP.`

segments.voice: The book opens by saying why it happened: it was "in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled," and "the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus." A foreign king, and the text sees God moving through him anyway. Help, again, from an unexpected place. Now listen to the shape of the decree. It isn't an order. It's an invitation: let him go up. Not everyone does. The text says the ones who rose up to go were all those whose spirit God had stirred. Others stay, and the text doesn't scold them. The people of each place help instead: they strengthen the travelers with silver and gold, goods and animals, and freewill offerings for the house of God. A return needs both, the ones who go and the ones who send them. Then Cyrus does one more thing. He brings out the vessels of the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar had carried off from Jerusalem, counts them out to a leader of Judah, and sends them home. A few days ago, in Daniel, a king drank wine from vessels like these. Now they're being packed for the road. The return doesn't begin with a wall or a Temple. It begins with going up, and carrying back what was taken.
screen: `GOD STIRRED UP A FOREIGN KING.` · `LET HIM GO UP: AN INVITATION.` · `THOSE AROUND THEM SENT GIFTS.` · then, large: `THE VESSELS GO HOME.` · then: `GOING UP, CARRYING BACK.`

segments.voice: Today's practice is to go back to one thing. Sit, and let your breathing find its own pace. Think of the vessels, packed for the road after years in a foreign treasury. Is there something of yours that got left somewhere along the way? A song your family sang. A recipe nobody makes anymore. A language you grew up hearing. A skill you set down. Don't scold yourself for the distance. The decree didn't. Just hold the thing in your mind, the way an exile might hold the name of a city. Then find the first step to carry it back, small enough to take today. If you pray, you can ask in words from your tradition for your spirit to be stirred. The bell holds the time.
The return. Cyrus's decree in Ezra 1: let him go up to Jerusalem, and build the house of the LORD. Today's word.
Your line: the return. Today, take the first small step back toward the thing you found, even five minutes' worth. Day eight hundred seventy-four.

howItsDone: Moving to the land of Israel is called aliyah, going up, the same picture of going up that Cyrus's decree uses, and Jews who move to Israel today are said to make aliyah.

original.note: Hebrew: and let him go up, from Cyrus's decree in Ezra 1:3.

trapdoor: what you thought: the return was a forced move back home.
what it means: a foreign king invites the exiles to go up and rebuild, and sends back the vessels taken from the Temple.
what a scholar hears: the text says God stirred Cyrus's spirit to fulfill Jeremiah's word, and stirred the spirits of those who went: one verb, a king and a people.

notes: The index hook gives 'around 538 BCE'. Under the claims rule the script gives only what Ezra 1:1 says, 'the first year of Cyrus king of Persia'; the date is left out of the spoken script and of the hook field (the meta index line keeps it).
Trapdoor: 'one verb' for God stirring Cyrus (1:1) and stirring the spirits of those who went (1:5): the KJV has 'stirred up' and 'raised'; the Hebrew uses the same verb (he'ir). Please confirm.
The link to Daniel 5's vessels ('vessels like these') is phrased loosely on purpose; Daniel 5:2 and Ezra 1:7 both describe vessels Nebuchadnezzar took from the Temple.
The leader of Judah who receives the vessels is Sheshbazzar (1:8), unnamed in the script.
Original: please verify the pointing of וְיַעַל in Ezra 1:3. howItsDone ties aliyah to this decree; Keeper please confirm.
